articles.title_orig: Fed official Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House firing hearing, citing bias
articles.title_zh: Fed official Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House firing hearing, citing bias
articles.content_orig:
Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook 's attorney on Tuesday gave the strongest signal yet that his client will not attend a hearing at the White House with a "committee of inquiry" investigating mortgage fraud allegations against Cook.
The committee established last month by President Donald Trump , who has previously tried to remove Cook from the central bank's board, is pretextual and poses a threat to the Fed, attorney Abbe Lowell wrote in a letter to presidential counsel Will Scharf.
"Governor Cook has no legal obligation to participate in an unfair hearing — and indeed, has a duty to the Federal Reserve to decline to participate in any proceeding that would undermine the institution's unique status and independence," Lowell wrote in the letter, which is dated Monday and was made public Tuesday.
The latest correspondence came nearly two weeks after the White House committee delayed its proposed hearing with Cook to Dec. 14 from Nov. 5. Lowell said that any hearing with Cook could not take place until at least December because of conflicts with her Fed duties.
While Lowell had raised strong concerns from the outset about the legitimacy of the committee, he initially said Cook "welcomes the opportunity to present the facts so she can clear her name."
But he has continued to cast doubts on both the committee's purpose and its composition of three executive branch officials, including National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett .
Lowell's tone sounded more hostile than ever in this week's letter, the first known to be sent by either party in the matter since the Republican Party's devastating losses in the midterm elections on Nov. 3.
He accused Scharf and the committee of seeking "only to manufacture 'cause' for a predetermined removal outcome."
Lowell highlighted two top concerns. First, he asserted that Hassett "is not competent to serve on any factfinding committee" because his prior comments about Cook "demonstrate that he has prejudged the issue."
Second, Lowell called it "fundamentally unfair" that the committee is demanding Cook hand over documents "immediately," while pledging to provide the governor with its own records just seven days before the hearing.
"Your and the Committee's failure to address these legitimate issues, over multiple weeks of back-and-forth correspondence, reinforces my prior observation: President Trump's decision to fire Governor Cook has already been made," Lowell wrote.
"Consequently, this Committee process appears to be a façade designed to obscure a predetermined decision to fire Governor Cook or to unreasonably manufacture a supposed 'adverse inference' if she does not participate in a process that does not comport with the requirements of a fair hearing," the lawyer wrote.
Lowell told Scharf that Cook would still be prepared to appear for a hearing if the White House "implements fair procedures." But the "ultimatums" Scharf gave in his last reply in early November "do not provide a productive path forward to enabling that participation," Lowell wrote.
The White House did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on Lowell's letter.
Trump, who frequently urges the Fed to lower interest rates, has long sought to fire Cook, an appointee of former President Joe Biden .
Cook, the first Black woman to serve on the Fed's Board of Governors, last voted to cut rates in December 2025, siding with the majority. The Fed unanimously voted to raise rates after its meeting in September.
Trump officials sent a criminal referral last year alleging Cook may have committed mortgage fraud by falsely claiming different properties as her primary residence in order to get more favorable terms. Cook adamantly denied wrongdoing, and, after Trump tried to fire her in August 2025, filed a lawsuit to block her removal.
The Supreme Court in June prevented Trump from firing Cook, but gave him a path to try again if additional legal steps were taken. In August, the White House told Cook it was reviving its efforts to fire her on mortgage-related grounds. In October, Trump signed a presidential memo establishing the committee of inquiry to investigate allegations that Cook lied on records related to "one or more mortgage instruments."

articles.title_orig: Sheinbaum and Xi meet in Shenzhen to mark a ‘new era,’ advance Mexico-China relations
articles.title_zh: Sheinbaum and Xi meet in Shenzhen to mark a ‘new era,’ advance Mexico-China relations
articles.content_orig:
In a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Tuesday, President Claudia Sheinbaum declared that her visit to China marks “a new era” in Mexico’s relationship with the East Asian country.
She also told the Chinese president and general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party she was “convinced” that the bilateral meeting would “strengthen collaboration” between the Mexican and Chinese governments and the Mexican and Chinese people. In subsequent remarks to reporters , Sheinbaum described her meeting with Xi as “very good” and “very, very frank.”
For his part, Xi told Sheinbaum that China and Mexico are “good friends” and that advancing relations is “important for both countries,” according to a readout published by China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs .
The two leaders and members of their respective cabinets met in Shenzhen ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders’ Meeting, which starts in the southern Chinese city on Wednesday. Sheinbaum previously met with Xi at the G20 leaders’ summit in Brazil in November 2024 .
In public remarks to Xi , Sheinbaum thanked the Chinese president for his invitation to the APEC CEO Summit, at which she spoke on Tuesday .
She noted that Mexico will host the APEC Leaders’ Meeting in 2028 and told Xi it would be a “pleasure” to welcome him to that event.
Sheinbaum said that the Mexico-China relationship is “the result of deep bonds of friendship and shared principles, such as cooperation, development and shared prosperity.”
“Mexico and China share a vision of development and prosperity, and our nations have strengthened their relationship in order to cooperate on a variety of issues,” she said.
“On this occasion, we are interested in strengthening cooperation in areas related to science and technology, agriculture, clean energy, water resources, health and, of course, culture and tourism,” Sheinbaum said.
According to a statement issued by Mexico’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (SRE), Sheinbaum and Xi “highlighted opportunities to deepen bilateral cooperation on health, river cleanup and restoration, sustainable water management, biodiversity conservation, waste management guided by circular economy principles , the fight against climate change and the development of resilient cities, as Shenzhen’s model shows.”
In China, Mexico’s environment minister takes notes on its waste-to-energy circular economy
“They also agreed to strengthen scientific cooperation by training talent, conducting joint research in strategic areas such as mathematics, agriculture, biotechnology and clean energy, and developing bilateral initiatives, including the Young Scientists Exchange Program,” the SRE said.
The ministry also said that Sheinbaum and Xi “expressed their desire to keep strengthening” the Mexico-China relationship through the two countries’ Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, which was launched by Xi and former Mexican President Enrique Peña Nieto in 2013 .
Mexico and China don’t have a free trade agreement, and the former country angered the latter when it imposed new and higher tariffs on Chinese goods at the start of 2026 .
Mexico’s tariffs on China — seen in part as an effort to appease U.S. President Donald Trump, who has accused Mexico of being a transshipment hub for Chinese goods — were not mentioned by the SRE or the Chinese Foreign Ministry in their statements.
The SRE did say that the Mexican and Chinese presidents “discussed opportunities to deepen trade,” adding that Sheinbaum “said Mexico is interested in moving toward a more balanced and diversified economic relationship.”
China’s exports to Mexico — which include electronic equipment and electric vehicles — are worth far more than its imports from Mexico, leaving it with a large trade surplus . Some imports from China pose a threat to Mexican manufacturing sectors, giving the Mexican government added incentive to impose higher tariffs on them.
Sheinbaum told reporters in Shenzhen that she and Xi had spoken about increasing Mexico’s exports of various products to China, “from avocados to tequila.”
Asked whether she and the Chinese president spoke about Mexico’s relationship with the United States, the president responded:
“The issue was raised, but we always talk about our trade agreement with the United States, and [say] that we will always do what is best for Mexico.”
The statement issued by the Chinese Foreign Ministry said that “given the complex and volatile global landscape, advancing China-Mexico relations at a higher level, across wider areas, and in greater depth is important for both countries as they implement their respective national development strategies and promote unity for strength among the Global South.”
The ministry said that in his meeting with Sheinbaum, “President Xi stressed that China and Mexico should first continue to treat each other with sincerity, deepen political mutual trust, keep growing bilateral relations in the right direction, enhance exchanges and cooperation in all areas and at all levels, and work together to ensure the success of events celebrating the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations next year.”
The Chinese Foreign Ministry also said that “Mexico firmly adheres to the one-China principle and attaches great importance to its relations with China.”
“In the course of implementing Plan México , Mexico is ready to strengthen cooperation with China in areas such as trade, investment, science and technology, manufacturing, artificial intelligence, agriculture and water conservancy and promote exchanges in health, education, culture and tourism, so as to elevate bilateral relations to a new height,” the ministry added.
While Mexico is clearly seeking to strengthen — and broaden — its relationship with China, Sheinbaum is mindful of the need to safeguard Mexico’s relationship with the United States, its largest trade partner. For example, the president — who will meet with Trump in Shenzhen on Wednesday — has made it clear that Mexico is not seeking a free trade agreement with China , the world’s second largest economy.
One apparent motive for China to seek closer ties with Mexico is the country’s proximity to Beijing’s foremost strategic rival — the United States.
In remarks to reporters after her meeting with Xi, Sheinbaum noted that a Chinese company is supplying trains to Mexico ( for the under-construction Mexico City-Pachuca railroad ) and reiterated that Mexico is “very interested” in learning more about China’s “ smart hospitals .”

— Quadratín México (@QuadratinMexico) November 17, 2026
She subsequently revealed that she asked Xi for a panda for the Chapultepec Zoo, located in Chapultepec Park in Mexico City.
One panda, a female called Xin Xin , already lives at the zoo. She was born at the Chapultepec Zoo in 1990.
Given that Mexico and China are on friendly terms and seeking even closer ties, it would appear likely that China will grant Sheinbaum’s request for a panda. According to Reuters , since its founding in 1949, “the People’s Republic of China has used panda diplomacy to boost its international image, either by gifting or lending pandas to foreign zoos as goodwill animal ambassadors.”

articles.title_orig: Nvidia earnings live: Nvidia posts Q3 beat, board says it will not reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.title_zh: Nvidia earnings live: Nvidia posts Q3 beat, board says it will not reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia shares closed marginally lower Tuesday as former CEO Jensen Huang released his first public statement since his resignation and the company prepares to report earnings after the bell.
The stock move Tuesday marked Nvidia's fourth straight daily decline.
In the statement, Huang said he is open to returning as Nvidia's CEO and that he is committed to cooperating with the board's investigation into his behavior.
"I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret," Huang said in a statement obtained by CNBC's David Faber . "I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation."
"If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO," Huang continued.
Huang resigned from Nvidia, the company's board announced on Thursday, following reports that he had a relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy. Huang told employees he had an affair in an email on Nov. 8. Outlets also reported that Huang also had an affair with a vice president at the company and an "intimate relationship" with an unnamed second employee.
Nvidia's stock slid 4% on Monday, bringing shares to their lowest close since July 1, 2025.
Lawmakers also announced Tuesday that Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter will appear before the same committees on Dec. 2.
Nvidia's stock slid 4% on Monday, bringing shares to their lowest close since July 1, 2025.
An online petition calling for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO drew more than 190,000 signatures , including Elon Musk . But Nvidia's board of directors is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC on Monday.
The chip giant is also facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips, which U.S. export controls restrict from going to China.
The U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, announced on Monday an interim final rule designed to prevent Chinese companies' remote access to AI chips.
Nvidia announced on Tuesday morning that its board had established a committee responsible for oversight of the company's national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management.
The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson and will include directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members, the company said in a statement.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang breaks silence after resigning from Nvidia, says he "would be honored" to return as CEO
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang breaks silence after resigning from Nvidia, says he "would be honored" to return as CEO
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang broke his silence after resigning from the company following revelations of multiple affairs, saying he'd be willing to return as its CEO.
"I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," Huang said in a statement Tuesday morning. "I created problems for the board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board's independent investigation."
He added, "If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."
Late Tuesday, however, Nvidia Chair Harvey Jones said the company's board doesn't intend to rehire Huang as chief executive. The company's search for a new chief is underway, he added, while noting that the board has "every confidence" in Kress' ability to lead the company. Jones said the company is considering both internal and external candidates to replace Huang.
Huang has gained support from more than 190,000 people, including several thousand Nvidia employees, who signed a petition to reinstate him. On Monday, President Trump suggested to reporters that he would support Huang returning to Nvidia.
"I would not mind seeing that," Mr. Trump said. Later, the president said he recommended former Apple CEO Tim Cook as Nvidia's next leader.
In his Tuesday statement, Huang thanked his allies for their support since his departure last week, saying that in addition to the public calls for him to return to the company, many "continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive and geopolitical dynamics."
Nvidia's board said on Tuesday that it has formed a committee to oversee its national security policies and ensure compliance with U.S. export controls. The former CEO has also agreed to appear before House lawmakers on Dec. 1 to address questions about a potential breach of national security amid an investigation into his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
The former CEO's return to Nvidia is unlikely, said Yorkville Ives & Co. technology analyst Dan Ives.
"In our view the sequencing is the tell: Jensen has conditioned his return on a board decision, and the board's first public act this week was to build a compliance structure around the issue that forced him out, which is not what a board preparing to reverse itself does," he said in a Tuesday research note.
Shares of Nvidia declined $2.63, or 1.7%, to $153.51. The stock has lost 16% of its value since Huang's extramarital relationships became public.
Caitlin  Yilek contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Fed Issues Possible Bank Run Warning As Outages Fuel Wild Nov. 17 ‘Blackout’ Theories
articles.title_zh: Fed Issues Possible Bank Run Warning As Outages Fuel Wild Nov. 17 ‘Blackout’ Theories
articles.content_orig:
By PHILLIP NIETO, US POLITICAL REPORTER
Published: 09:27 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 14:17 EST, 17 November 2026
JD Vance has told Americans they do not need a bunker or a food stockpile, days after a global email collapse, a nationwide ground stop and a banking meltdown.
‘A lot of my friends have reached out asking if they should prepare to build a bunker or stock up on food and water,’ the vice president told Fox News host Laura Ingraham on Monday night.
‘We don’t see a crisis coming down,’ Vance added, ‘but you have to be prepared for everything.’
‘We want to make sure we prevent the worst outcomes, but we’re also prepared for the worst outcomes,’ he continued.
Ingraham had asked him point blank whether Americans should be prepping for a major global catastrophe. It comes after Britain and France have told their own citizens to keep days of food and water at home.
Vance brushed off the reporting behind the question, including accounts of Pentagon bases preparing to run off the grid for 90 days, as ‘just basic good government, making sure that our military is prepared, God forbid, if there was a crisis.’
Meanwhile, Google has warned corporate America that hackers powered by artificial intelligence are running autonomous attacks across major systems.
The company's report released on Monday claims these AI hackers can constantly work around security patches, write working exploits and fire them at online servers.
Vance has told Americans they do not need a bunker or a food stockpile, days after a global email collapse, a nationwide ground stop and a banking meltdown
Google has warned corporate America that hackers powered by artificial intelligence are now running autonomous attacks across major systems
Tens of thousands of travelers were left stranded over the weekend after the FAA issued a nationwide grounding for all flights
Google drew no connection between its findings and last week’s failures, and federal officials say they have found no evidence that anyone attacked anything.
Moreover, Hackers have compromised some of the world’s most visited websites in a sweeping cyberattack targeting users’ money and credit card details.
Security researchers identified malicious code in website tools used by 178 organizations, including Zoom, CNN, the BBC, HSBC, Equifax, Salesforce, Peacock, IKEA, Fox News, NPR, the ASPCA and Invisalign.
The attack, detected Monday evening, targeted Optimizely, a service companies use to test different website layouts and features.
Microsoft’s Outlook, Teams and Copilot services collapsed on Thursday and stayed down for users in 74 countries into the weekend.
On Friday, approxiatemately 10,000 flights were disrupted after the Federal Aviation Administration halted departures across the country, the second nationwide ground stop since the September 11 attacks.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has blamed a router that contractor L3Harris Technologies installed at a remote FAA radio site in Arkansas.
It flooded a network still running on equipment built in 2001 and scheduled for replacement in 2006.
Duffy called FBI Director Kash Patel to pull agents into the investigation, the router now sits in a laboratory in Florida, and the FAA has switched off the broadcast function on all 69 of the same devices across the national airspace.
By Monday, banks had been affected by the the outages as thousands of customers at Chase, Wells Fargo, US Bank, Capital One, Truist and Bank of America reporting they could not see their balances or move cash.
United Airlines also delayed its own departures that same afternoon when pilots lost the weight and balance figures they need to leave the gate, stopping hundreds of flights.

articles.title_orig: The Nvidia Scandal Is Only Half the Story of China’s AI Workarounds
articles.title_zh: The Nvidia Scandal Is Only Half the Story of China’s AI Workarounds
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Former Nvidia boss Jensen Huang has said he would be “honoured” to return to the company after he was ousted in the wake of a scandal.
Mr Huang resigned from the chipmaker last week, amid a wave of scandal after he admitted to an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy as well as a subordinate at Nvidia . Since then, petitions and supporters have called for him to return – but the company has said that it is not interested in inviting him back.
Nonetheless, Mr Huang signalled he would be willing to return and that he would work with an investigation into the incident. But he suggested that the decision was up to the board and whether it thought his return would be “in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America”.
“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in his first public statement since he resigned on 12 November over revelations of extramarital affairs that intensified scrutiny of the chip firm's China business. Mr Huang had not been quoted in Nvidia’s original statement about his departure, though it thanked him for his “profound” contributions to the company, and he has been silent since.
“I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation,” he said in the new statement.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Mr Huang's statement, but multiple reports have suggested that its board is not planning to reappoint him. Nvidia shares ⁠pared some declines and were last down 1 per cent.
More than 180,000 people have signed a petition demanding Huang’s return, Elon Musk has thrown his support behind the effort, ⁠and US President Donald Trump said he would not mind seeing Huang reinstated as CEO. Thousands of people identifying themselves as Nvidia employees have joined the call, even as governance experts and some investors warn that bringing him back before investigations are complete could expose the company to fresh risks.
The groundswell of support for Huang has turned a corporate succession story into a test of whether Nvidia can separate itself from a founder whose influence stretches across its employees — some fiercely loyal to the former CEO — and shareholders, Silicon Valley, the Taiwanese supply chain and Washington.
Taiwan's tallest skyscraper, Taipei 101, was illuminated on Monday with messages including "Taiwan Loves Jensen." Some prominent shareholders such as Atreides ⁠Management's Gavin Baker and Altimeter Capital Management CEO Brad Gerstner have urged Nvidia not to rush to replace him ​before ⁠all the facts are known.
Earlier on Tuesday, before Mr Huang’s statement, Nvidia created a board-level ​committee ⁠to oversee national security and export controls, its first major governance move since he left.
Mr Huang's relationships have raised questions about whether Nvidia's oversight kept pace with its rapid growth and increasing importance to US national security. The crisis had erased more ⁠than $400 billion from the company's market value by Monday's close.
The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, ​a former Goldman Sachs ⁠vice chair, Nvidia said. Directors Stephen Neal, former CEO of ‌law firm Cooley, and John Dabiri, a Caltech professor, will also serve on the committee.
Donald Trump welcomed the move, calling the launch of a national security initiative a good idea.
In the full statement, posted on X, Mr Huang thanked the public for its support and admitted to having made “serious mistakes”. He also included a message to his family, in which he suggested they were offering him “support”.
“Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me,” he wrote.
“I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia.
“I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.
“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.
“Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.”

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang scandal fuels bipartisan push to block AI chip sales to China
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang scandal fuels bipartisan push to block AI chip sales to China
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia warned its customers that new legislation on Chinese companies remotely accessing its artificial-intelligence chips could expose it and them to U.S. "legal action," sources told CNBC.
The chip giant is facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips, which U.S. export controls restrict from going to China.
Nvidia messaged chip buyers in recent months to caution that the proposed Remote Access Security Act, or RASA, would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services in the same way as physical hardware, potentially exposing both parties to legal risk, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter. The people asked not to be named while discussing private communications.
It also said that, for now, it would not sell its chips to customers who rent more than 50% of the graphics processing units, or GPUs, to Chinese companies, the people said.
Separately, the Financial Times reported earlier this month that Nvidia verbally told data-center clients to direct at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese customers under future contracts.
Regulators have had limited powers to control companies' access to those chips through cloud services hosted overseas.
RASA passed the House of Representatives in January but has not yet passed the Senate. Remote access to the chips has provoked the ire of President Donald Trump 's administration, which has sought to keep the chips out of China to maintain the U.S. lead in the AI race.
CNBC reported on Nov. 5 that Chinese lab Moonshot AI sought access to Nvidia chips through data centers in Europe. The Trump administration previously singled the company out, accusing it in July of accessing the chips through centers in East Asia.
The U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, announced on Monday an interim final rule designed to prevent Chinese companies' remote access to AI chips.
Nvidia and BIS did not respond to a request for comment.
On Sunday, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia after Jensen Huang 's shock departure as CEO, amid reports of an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. authorities reportedly suspect of spying for China.
Bessent suggested other Nvidia executives should face scrutiny over the chip giant's compliance with export controls.
"I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?" Bessent told Fox News.
In an August securities filing , Nvidia said it sought to "strictly comply with all applicable export control regulators" but did not have "physical control of our products after sale" and relied on its customers' and partners' compliance programs.
Huang has been asked to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3.

articles.title_orig: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.
Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort.
The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before".
Meanwhile in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said traffic had partially resumed on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - after they had been closed following Russian strikes overnight.
Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good.
While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight.
The Crimean Bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014.
The $3.6bn (£2.7bn) piece of infrastructure is widely seen in Russia and Ukraine as Putin's personal pet project: His close tycoon friend Arkady Rotenberg built it, and then Putin personally opened it by driving a lorry over it in May 2018.
In Ukraine, the much-hated bridge is seen as one of the main symbols of Russia's continuing occupation of Ukrainian lands.
"We're drinking champagne!" Andrii, an engineer who lives in Kyiv, told the BBC.
He said the latest attack would "deal a very heavy blow to the morale of the Russians".
Some Ukrainians are concerned that Putin might now respond by carrying out even more attacks against civilian infrastructure, but Andrii said: "I don't think the Russians can make things much worse; they're already pounding us every single night with everything they've got."
The damage after the overnight attack, involving cruise missiles and drones, appeared to be far more severe than during previous strikes on the bridge, with a large arched section apparently destroyed.
Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below.
Zelensky said the strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective".
He said several types of Ukrainian drones as well as the country's Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles were fired overnight during a "pivotal stage".
The Ukrainian president also said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and Russia's transport ministry later said some rail services resumed.
Ukraine's state security service SBU said its operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders".
Meanwhile, Ukraine's military said the roadway on the bridge is "out of action", with no vehicle able to cross it, and the railway section is still standing, but with a damaged arch.
The Kremlin said Putin had been briefed on the overnight attack. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to China.
Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations".
For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry.
Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday.
In Kyiv, loud explosions were heard just before midnight on Monday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water supplies.
On Tuesday, Zelensky said four ballistic missiles had targeted the Southern Bridge, and another three had been fired on the Northern Bridge.
Some of Kyiv's above-ground metro services were also damaged in the overnight attacks, local officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters.
Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River, connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city.
Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the central Cherkasy region, according to local officials.
The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear, though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly.
The collapse of the arched section has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired.
However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Kyiv has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar.
This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo.
There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack.
Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area.
In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel.
This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for the Russian-occupied ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdyansk.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control.

articles.title_orig: Stock Market News, Nov. 17, 2026: Dow ends down 850 points, S&P 500 and Nasdaq also plunge as tech names come under further pressure ahead of Nvidia’s earnings
articles.title_zh: Stock Market News, Nov. 17, 2026: Dow ends down 850 points, S&P 500 and Nasdaq also plunge as tech names come under further pressure ahead of Nvidia’s earnings
articles.content_orig:
U.S. equities tumbled on Tuesday, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite hitting its lowest level in roughly seven months, as traders sold off semiconductor names ahead of Nvidia's much-anticipated earnings report.
Reports of a National Security Agency network outage added to recent jitters about the stability of the country's technology infrastructure and helped weigh on the market, traders said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 848.75 points, or 1.64%, to end at 50,759.42. It dropped more than 1,000 points at its session low. The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53, for its lowest closing level since late July. The broad market index sank as low as 1.7% earlier in the session.
The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.74%. At one point during Tuesday's session, it sank by as much as roughly 2.1% to touch its lowest level since April.
Major averages fell to their lows of the day following the report from CNN that said a classified network used by the spy agency had gone down, citing six people familiar with the matter. CNN's sources said there was no evidence that it was a cyberattack.
The NSA later in the day put out a statement saying the agency "experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance." The agency added that "mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational."
Traders said the report helped take equities lower, though the losses were contained. This outage is latest in a string of incidents that have left people on edge including the FAA ground stop over the weekend, Microsoft's Outlook outage last week and some recent issues with banking apps.
Nvidia shares ended the session 0.5% lower amid investors' handwringing ahead of the company's earnings report due after the closing bell. However, the stock got a short-lived boost earlier in the session after Jensen Huang said he would be open to returning as CEO if the company's board thought that was in the best interest of shareholders.
"Nvidia should report strong results and guidance, but [it] is unlikely to be able to give investors solid answers to the questions heavily weighing on the stock [regarding] leadership and investigations around export controls," Ross Mayfield, investment strategist at Baird, told CNBC. "Strong demand might stabilize things, but the next leg higher will need some clarification around the 2028 and beyond outlook."
Other tech players ended the day in negative territory but well off their session lows, with Micron Technology sliding 0.9%. Advanced Micro Devices slipped 0.2%, while Intel was down 0.5%.
Microsoft shares were down 2%.
Neocloud stock Iren shed more than 3%. Nebius lost 1%. Investor Steve Eisman told CNBC earlier in the day that these stocks were among the names with the most to lose if the Huang scandal causes Nvidia to pull back its financing of the AI ecosystem.
U.S. equities closed lower on Tuesday.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 848.75 points, or 1.64%, lower at 50,759.42. It fell more than 1,000 points at its session low.
The S&P 500 shed 1.03% to end the session at 7,340.53, for its lowest closing level since late July. The broad market index sank as low as 1.73% earlier in the session.
The Nasdaq Composite was down 0.74% to 24,328.38 at the closing bell. At one point, it sank by as much as roughly 2.1% to hit its lowest level since April.
The VIX volatility index , a gauge of how much the S&P 500 might move in the next 30 days based on options trading, rose as much as 21% to an intraday high of 27.73, the highest since Nov. 6.
The VIX is now on track to rise for a fourth consecutive day for the first time since August 28.
Recent market volatility doesn't change UBS' conviction in the opportunity in artificial intelligence or its constructive view on diversified equities.
Investors weighing AI demand and the elevated capital expenditures from tech companies have sent stocks lower.
"Still, for the sell-off to indicate a lasting deterioration in the AI investment cycle, we would need to see weakening compute demand, slowing AI- related revenue growth, poor capacity utilization, or tighter financial conditions constraining spending by the largest technology platforms, Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, chief investment officer for Americas, said in a note Tuesday.
Breadth of selling will also matter, and there is no evidence of that yet. Underlying demand for computing capacity also remains robust, he noted.
"We therefore continue to see potential for gains in broad equity markets over the next six to 12 months, supported by resilient economic growth and corporate earnings," Hoffmann-Burchardi wrote. "Near-term volatility reinforces the importance of selectivity and disciplined portfolio construction rather than a broadly defensive stance."
A CNN report Tuesday that a classified network used by the National Security Agency is down was just the latest to hit a stock market that's been battered lately by negative headlines. These include the FAA ground stop over the weekend, as well as Microsoft's Outlook outage last week.
"Any one of the stories that have have broken over the course of the last week or so would be enough to cause the market jitters. But when you compound that by having multiple stories — whether it's today's NSA report or the FAA ground halt or Microsoft Outlook being down for two days or Chase Bank ATMs not working — aggregate all of those, and it's easy for the human mind to get to a place where there must be something larger at play here," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth. "What's causing the market to have the kind of drawdowns that it's having today, it's just that aggregate of the compounding of bizarre stories that just have become too much of a headwind, at least in the near term," he added.
Investors may not be moved by Nvidia's upcoming earnings results, according to Megan Horneman, chief investment officer at Verdence Capital Advisors.
"I don't think there's going to be anything surprising from the earnings report," she told CNBC. "I don't know that we're even going to get much forward-looking information that people may be trying to get information on."
Horneman expects uncertainty to persist for the technology sector as investors assess what the trade could look like after "parts of Nvidia start to unwind."
"We're just stuck in this, I think, panic type of stage right now, and I don't know how far it will go," she said.
Another strong round of economic data, particularly on the consumer side, has led Goldman Sachs to take up its growth forecast.
The firm now sees  fourth quarter gross domestic product accelerating by a 2.4% annualized pace, up 0.6 percentage point from its prior outlook. Moreover, Goldman raised its backward-looking expectation for the third quarter, now looking for 3.8% growth from the period, which would be 0.4 percentage point higher than the advance estimate from the Commerce Department.
At the core of the more optimistic outlook is a retail sales report Tuesday that showed receipts up 0.2% in October — 0.6% when excluding autos and when focusing on the components that feed directly to GDP.
"The strength of today's report continues to reflect the resilience of the US consumer this year, as boosts from tax refunds and positive wealth effects from equity market gains have more than offset the drag from higher energy prices," Goldman chief economist Jan Hatzius said in a note.
Selling was broad across Wall Street midday Tuesday as declining stocks outnumbered advancers by nearly 3 to 1 on both the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq.
Declining volume accounted for roughly 69% of total NYSE volume and 71% on the Nasdaq, according to FactSet data.
On the NYSE, 1,924 stocks declined while only 700 rose. For Nasdaq, decliners totaled 3,036, compared with 1,141 advancers.
New lows also outpaced new highs. The NYSE recorded 362 new lows against just 20 new highs, while the Nasdaq logged 679 new lows versus 38 new highs.
— Deena Zaidi and Scott Schnipper

articles.title_orig: Following Microsoft Outlook, Teams, Gmail outage has hit. Marriott down too
articles.title_zh: Following Microsoft Outlook, Teams, Gmail outage has hit. Marriott down too
articles.content_orig:
Google said Tuesday that it had found no evidence of a widespread disruption to its Gmail service, despite thousands of users reporting problems accessing or receiving emails. “We’re not currently seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption. Our teams monitor service health closely, and real-time status updates are always available on the Google Workspace Status Dashboard,” a Google spokesperson told Anadolu. The statement came after outage-tracking website Downdetector recorded more than 2,800 reports of problems with Gmail by 12 noon US Eastern Time (1700GMT). Most complaints reportedly involved difficulties receiving emails, while some users pointed to problems accessing the service. Google’s official Workspace Status Dashboard did not list any active Gmail disruptions as of 1.45 pm ET. The reports come amid a series of technology disruptions across the US in recent days, including an outage affecting Microsoft’s Outlook email service and a telecommunications failure that prompted the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to temporarily halt flights nationwide. There is no evidence that the reported Gmail problems are connected to those incidents.

articles.title_orig: California bans Waymo autonomous vehicles from state freeways, saying they pose an 'imminent hazard'
articles.title_zh: California bans Waymo autonomous vehicles from state freeways, saying they pose an 'imminent hazard'
articles.content_orig:
Waymo is temporarily pausing driverless rides on freeways in all its markets after California’s Department of Motor Vehicles said Tuesday that its self-driving vehicles can’t use state freeways for now, citing safety concerns following a series of incidents.
Waymo has allowed its cars to operate on freeways in five of its 13 cities in the US: San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin, according to the company.
California’s DMV said the autonomous cars pose “imminent hazard to public safety” following at least two recent incidents involving the vehicles. In one occasion, three Waymo vehicles entered an active construction zone along US Route 101, while another incident involved California Highway Patrol vehicles on Highway 280, the department said.
In the latter, a Waymo vehicle attempted to pass patrol cars conducting a traffic break earlier this month, CNN affiliate KGO reported.
According to the agency, Waymo vehicles have made “recurrent incursions” into active construction zones, putting workers, other vehicles and equipment at risk.
“We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations,” a Waymo spokesperson said.
The company noted the US Route 101 incident did not result in any injuries or collisions.
This is the second time this year Waymo has faced highway restrictions in the state, according to CNN affiliate KGO . The company paused freeway operations in May in San Francisco and Los Angeles to improve its vehicles’ response to construction zones. The previous restriction followed similar incidents that month, according to the California DMV.
A CNN analysis earlier this year found hundreds of incidents in which robotaxis allegedly made dangerous maneuvers and struggled with obstacles that humans instinctively handle. They ran red lights, drove into oncoming traffic and active crime scenes, failed to abide by emergency road closures and came within inches of pedestrians lawfully crossing the street.
Waymo data said its vehicles are involved in 95% fewer crashes resulting in serious injuries or worse than human drivers.
The restriction went into effect on November 11 and will remain in effect until Waymo addresses the safety lapses, the agency said.
This story has been updated with additional information.

articles.title_orig: Trump’s New A.I. Chip Rules Rattle Southeast Asia
articles.title_zh: Trump’s New A.I. Chip Rules Rattle Southeast Asia
articles.content_orig:
Revelations about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy have reinvigorated a congressional push to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence technology.
Federal lawmakers are pushing to include several measures to tighten export controls on advanced chips and related technologies in the final version of the National Defense Authorization Act. Congress is expected to consider the must-pass package that authorizes defense funding in December. Those proposals were included as amendments to an earlier version of the NDAA, which Senate Democrats blocked in July and have not been adopted by either congressional chamber in the interim.
The measures could give Congress authority to review chip sales to adversaries, empower the Commerce Department to track advanced AI chips and block the sale of key chipmaking tools to China-linked businesses.
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer , D-N.Y., renewed his calls for their passage from the Senate floor on Monday.
"My colleagues and I have been advocating for these bills and pushing Trump to get tougher on Chinese export controls for years," Schumer said. "His administration has shown time and time again that it is completely disinterested in enforcing export controls."
Schumer and other key players argue that such legislation is crucial to protecting the U.S. lead in AI technology. Allowing China access to advanced AI chips could undermine national security, proponents of the bills say.
Huang resigned from Nvidia, the world's leading supplier of advanced AI chips, last week after reports that he had several extramarital affairs , including one with a Chinese business executive whom U.S. intelligence believed could be a spy.
The affair raised questions about whether Huang might have disclosed sensitive information to the woman, named Alice Huang, who worked until 2025 at a Singaporean company called Megaspeed that U.S. agencies are investigating for allegedly routing U.S. chips to Chinese firms .
Three bills — the AI Overwatch Act , the MATCH Act , and the Chip Security Act — were included in the amendment package of the Senate version of the NDAA that stalled in the summer . The House narrowly passed its version of the NDAA, which did not include the AI measures, in July.
Now, there's new urgency to include them in the final package. The bills are largely complementary of one another, all aimed at blocking U.S. adversaries from obtaining the most advanced American chips.
"I think this incident, as troubling as it is, really highlights the need for export controls and a policy that is designed to keep America in the lead," House China Select Committee Chair John Moolenaar , R-Mich., told reporters Wednesday.
But wrangling a deal on the NDAA could prove challenging.
The fiscal year 2027 NDAA would authorize spending more than $1.1 trillion, a massive sum that has made some Democrats queasy. The White House asked for $1.5 trillion in total military spending in its annual budget, as the Iran war has boosted defense costs. The 2027 proposal is about 25% bigger than the roughly $890 billion 2026 measure.
In addition, the war with Iran has prompted some Democrats to take issue with the annual defense package. The Trump administration has executed the war without congressional approval, which is typically sought for major military action, and its price tag continues to rise in the war's ninth month. Some Democrats have argued that it is irresponsible to grant the Pentagon a record budget amid such a conflict.
Congress has passed the NDAA without fail for 65 consecutive years — meaning a failure this year would carry historical weight. The annual defense bill is typically ironed out by legislative leaders from the House and Senate meeting to come to a compromise agreement between the bills their chambers have approved.
Since the Huang scandal broke, lawmakers have escalated their pitches for export control legislation to be included. Now members of congressional leadership from both parties are joining the last-minute push to advance new export controls.
The AI Overwatch Act would codify President Donald Trump's bans on exporting the most powerful AI chips to U.S. adversaries, including China, Iran, Cuba and North Korea, and would give Congress authority to review and block specific export licenses. The bill also aims to fast-track the export of U.S. AI technology to allies for trusted U.S. companies.
Rep. Brian Mast , R-Fla., who leads the House Foreign Affairs Committee, has touted the MATCH Act, a proposal that would block sales of chipmaking equipment to companies located in "adversary countries." The MATCH Act advanced out of the Foreign Affairs Committee in April but never got a vote on the House floor.
The bill would also create consequences for allied countries that do not follow suit in imposing similar export restrictions on semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The move is intended to harmonize the U.S. and its allies in blocking adversaries from obtaining the equipment.
Mast said that and similar proposals have gained momentum recently, in part due to support from the Trump administration.
But the administration has been inconsistent on the topic of export controls on advanced AI chips. In December 2025, Trump authorized the sale of Nvidia's H200 chips to approved customers in China under pressure from Huang , who frequently lobbied Congress and the administration against banning chip sales to China.
On Monday, the Commerce Department announced a new rule aiming to close a loophole that has let Chinese companies lease Nvidia 's advanced computing power from data centers in third countries.
That announcement came amid scrutiny from lawmakers, and some people within Trump's Cabinet, of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick 's relationship with Huang and Nvidia. Cantor Fitzgerald, the financial services firm two of Lutnick's sons run and that he previously led, has had heavy client positions in Nvidia .
"We will protect National Security, create American Jobs, and keep America's lead in AI," Trump said in a Truth Social post after announcing that he would allow the H200 to be exported to China for a 25% cut. "President Xi responded positively!"
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries , D-N.Y., last week also expressed support for the legislative measures.
"There are provisions currently in the Senate version of the NDAA that will restrict chip access to China that I strongly support, and I think we're going to work hard to make sure that these provisions make it into the final version of the National Defense Authorization Act," Jeffries said at a press conference .
Republican leadership has been more tight-lipped on the proposals, which also include the Chip Security Act that would require location verification of advanced AI chips. The bill would do that by requiring export-controlled advanced chips or products that contain advanced chips to have a location tracker installed.
Senate Majority Leader John Thune , R-S.D., has not publicly weighed in on the proposals. His office also did not respond to a request for comment.
Speaker of the House Mike Johnson , R-La., told reporters Thursday he favored limiting chip exports to China. "‌I think there's a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take. Especially in ‌the light of ​recent developments, it ​makes ​sense," he said.

articles.title_orig: Wall Street ends lower ahead of Nvidia earnings, Anthropic debut
articles.title_zh: Wall Street ends lower ahead of Nvidia earnings, Anthropic debut
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia shares closed marginally lower Tuesday as former CEO Jensen Huang released his first public statement since his resignation and the company prepares to report earnings after the bell.
The stock move Tuesday marked Nvidia's fourth straight daily decline.
In the statement, Huang said he is open to returning as Nvidia's CEO and that he is committed to cooperating with the board's investigation into his behavior.
"I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret," Huang said in a statement obtained by CNBC's David Faber . "I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation."
"If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO," Huang continued.
Huang resigned from Nvidia, the company's board announced on Thursday, following reports that he had a relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy. Huang told employees he had an affair in an email on Nov. 8. Outlets also reported that Huang also had an affair with a vice president at the company and an "intimate relationship" with an unnamed second employee.
Nvidia's stock slid 4% on Monday, bringing shares to their lowest close since July 1, 2025.
Lawmakers also announced Tuesday that Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter will appear before the same committees on Dec. 2.
Nvidia's stock slid 4% on Monday, bringing shares to their lowest close since July 1, 2025.
An online petition calling for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO drew more than 190,000 signatures , including Elon Musk . But Nvidia's board of directors is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC on Monday.
The chip giant is also facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips, which U.S. export controls restrict from going to China.
The U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, announced on Monday an interim final rule designed to prevent Chinese companies' remote access to AI chips.
Nvidia announced on Tuesday morning that its board had established a committee responsible for oversight of the company's national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management.
The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson and will include directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members, the company said in a statement.

articles.title_orig: Facing Criticism, Trump Administration Says It’s Investigating Megaspeed
articles.title_zh: Facing Criticism, Trump Administration Says It’s Investigating Megaspeed
articles.content_orig:
The chip-smuggling controversy swirling around Nvidia centers on one company : Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing provider that, according to several media reports, is suspected of funneling advanced AI processors to Chinese companies.
While details of what Megaspeed is alleged to have done remain murky, experts say the case shows how Chinese firms rely on Southeast Asia to skirt U.S. trade controls.
“Chinese firms can access data centers in Singapore and Malaysia—and their computing capacity—without having to import restricted semiconductors,” Ja Ian Chong, a political science expert from the National University of Singapore (NUS), tells Fortune . “But the ease of shipping [chips] through Singapore and Malaysia also makes them attractive for firms and people who wish to circumvent U.S. controls.”
Washington restricts the export of Nvidia’s top-end Blackwell and Rubin chips to China, out of fear Beijing could use them to supercharge its AI ambitions .
According to The Information , Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, used her personal relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to move at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips through Megaspeed and its Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix.
Singapore says it is investigating Megaspeed for “suspected breaches of our domestic laws,” but it separately rejected reports that its authorities were investigating Alice Huang over the espionage allegations. U.S. officials had also been investigating Megaspeed for potential export-control violations.
Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing; Nvidia has previously claimed that it found no evidence of illicit chip transfers.
Nvidia’s board said in a Nov. 8 statement that it was initiating an independent investigation into whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, though it added it had no reason to believe “either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised.” The board said it “prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.”
Following reports that Huang conducted a second affair, this time with an Nvidia executive, the chipmaker’s board is now considering removing Huang as CEO, the Wall Street Journal reports.
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based neocloud that supplies AI computing power. Originally incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International, a Chinese gaming firm with ties to state-backed investors, the company changed its name to Megaspeed in early 2023, the same year that Alice Huang joined the company.
Another Singapore-registered firm, Swiftdata, acquired Megaspeed in November 2023. Alice Huang stepped down as Megaspeed’s managing director, while Singaporean businessman Tan Yong Pong—who owns Swiftdata —became its sole director. (Tan owns another Singapore-registered company, Monster Investment.)
In 2024, Tan established Speedmatrix, a Malaysia-based subsidiary of Megaspeed, which was reportedly used to receive shipments of Nvidia chips. According to the New York Times , between June 2024 and June 2025, Speedmatrix received over 200 shipments of restricted Nvidia technology.
These chips—which are subject to U.S. restrictions on sales to China—were eventually used to power data centers built by Shanghai Century Litong, a Chinese firm in which Alice’s younger sister, Huang Yu, is a founding shareholder, according to The Information . The firm, which builds data centers in the Chinese cities of Shanghai and Shenzhen, then provides high-performance AI computing capacity to Chinese tech giants including Alibaba and Tencent .
“AI chip distributors and resellers often spend too little effort vetting customers, usually relying on paperwork the customer provides,” notes Erich Grunewald, a senior researcher at the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy (IAPS), a U.S. nonpartisan think tank.
Malaysia has been one of Southeast Asia’s biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, drawing $94 billion in data center investments between 2021 and mid-2026, including from global tech hyperscalers like Google, AWS and Microsoft . “Malaysia has ample land and relatively cheap electricity and water, at least for now,” Chong notes. “The fact that it sits next to key submarine cables also makes it attractive as a spot for data centers.”
Singapore, on the other hand, is favored by multinationals for its open economy, stable political environment and business-friendly policies. Many AI firms, including U.S. firms Anthropic and OpenAI , have chosen to house their APAC headquarters there.
Companies like Megaspeed typically offer two routes to restricted silicon. The first is renting out chips already housed in data centers in Singapore and Malaysia—which, under current rules, is legal. The second is buying chips through front companies and shipping them to China, potentially in violation of U.S. export controls.
(Megaspeed reportedly did both: it set up data center operations in Sedenak Tech Park in the Malaysian state of Johor , and according to the reports , also shuttled chips to Shanghai Century Litong’s facilities in China.)
Under current U.S. export rules, it is legal to give Chinese companies access to AI processors housed outside of China—though previous deals have invited regulatory scrutiny. On Nov. 3, The Financial Times reported that Oracle had canceled a $7 billion deal to grant Tencent access to 100,000 AI chips in data centers across Southeast Asia after U.S. officials raised concerns. The FT also reported that Nvidia is telling cloud computing clients they must sell at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese companies.
The U.S. House of Representatives passed a law—the Remote Access Security Act —that would close the loophole allowing Chinese companies to use AI processors housed in other countries; the bill is now before the U.S. Senate.
Both Singapore and Malaysia have cracked down on chip smuggling. In addition to its investigation of Megaspeed, the Singaporean government last year charged three individuals with fraud after they diverted AI servers bound for Singapore to Malaysia instead.
In October, Malaysian customs officials seized $12.1 million worth of advanced AI chips at Kuala Lumpur International Airport. Initial investigations found the 30 servers—falsely declared as electronic components—were being transferred from one Asian country to another, though officials declined to say which.
Megaspeed, however, has denied the allegations . “There has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities, and this demonstrates that we are a compliant and legitimate company,” it wrote in a statement last December. “We operate fully within the bounds of all applicable export control regulations and maintain the highest standards of legal and ethical conduct.”
Chong says the escalating AI arms race between the U.S. and China means both Beijing and Washington will subject third parties like Singapore and Malaysia to deeper scrutiny to keep their own technology from leaking.
“Both Singapore and Malaysia will want to continue to benefit from trust by Beijing and Washington for as long as they can,” concludes Chong. “But they may face greater suspicion, scrutiny, restrictions and even punishment from one or both major powers going forward, and perceptions that they are unreliable or duplicitous partners will only increase such pressure.”
Angelica Ang is a Singapore-based journalist who covers the Asia-Pacific region.

articles.title_orig: How Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule
articles.title_zh: How Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule
articles.content_orig:
With the SpaceX satellite system faltering, Ukraine’s military launched a surprise, multi-pronged attack to take down vital bridge to Crimea
A t 10pm on Monday evening a Ukrainian soldier scrawled a message on a kamikaze drone. It said simply: “The bridge is fucked.” He then added: “We will stand and Moscow will fall.” It was a freezing night, with a bright starry sky and no clouds. Lines of ice had formed on the drone’s bulky wings. Soon, it would be hurtling towards its target – about 500km to the south.
Typically the soldiers who gathered in this muddy field in central Ukraine were attacking oil refineries deep inside Russia. In recent months the work had become almost mundane: they had hit so many of them. The objective that evening, however, was unique. It was a structure personally associated with Vladimir Putin and his grandiose imperial ambitions.
“We knew what the target was. Everyone was enthusiastic and excited,” one person who took part in the special operation, using the pseudonym “Leon”, told the Guardian. His 7th Deep Strike Centre is part of “Magyar’s Birds”, a brigade named after the call sign of its founder, Robert Brovdi, the head of Ukraine’s unmanned systems forces . Leon said: “Nobody gets excited any more about oil refineries. This was different.”
The soldiers got ready to launch, then watched the biplane-like drone, laden with explosives, disappear across the southern Ukrainian steppe.
Over the next four hours, hundreds of attack drones followed the same linear path, flying first over land and then over the Black Sea. In the early hours of the morning they arrived at their destination: the Kerch bridge connecting occupied Crimea with Russia. Putin opened the monumental road and rail crossing in 2018 , driving across it in a Kamaz truck. This was four years after his undercover troops – known as little green men – seized the peninsula.
Russian propagandists had described the bridge as impregnable. It was, they said, an edifice as strong and unyielding as their country’s iron leader. For Ukraine , by contrast, it was a hated symbol of Russian arrogance and colonial thinking. Also, officials pointed out, it was illegal. Twice Kyiv had tried to blow it up – with a truck bomb in 2022, and a sea drone the following year.
On this occasion, the Ukrainian military’s careful, multi-stage plan worked perfectly. “It was a well-coordinated operation. Waves of drones started from different locations. The goal was to overwhelm Russia’s well-organised air defence system, rather than the bridge itself,” Leon explained.
As expected, the initial salvo tied up Russia’s local defences. According to insiders, Ukraine then launched a second drone wave. Its function was crucial and different: to act as a relay system for radio signals. Previously, Ukrainian units had used Starshield, the military equivalent of Starlink, for mid-range strikes on occupied territory. Elon Musk’s SpaceX owns the satellite internet network, which is overseen by the Pentagon and the Trump administration.
Ten days ago, however, limits were mysteriously imposed on Ukrainian drones, so they could no longer fly at above 161 km/h (100 mph) . SpaceX insists there is no slowdown – a statement Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, says is untrue . On Monday night, it appears Kyiv bypassed US restrictions by setting up its own extraordinary and innovative real-time video and radio connection.
Once the relay was in place, a third wave of attacks could begin. This time they featured Flamingos, a potent Ukrainian-made cruise missile capable of carrying 1,000kg of explosives – enough to seriously damage the bridge. An unknown number of missiles – some reports say at least four – were launched from southern Ukraine and sent towards Crimea.
A video from one of the Flamingos shows it drawing inexorably towards the target. The onboard camera captures a ghostly night-time scene. The crossing looms into view against a grisaille background. Suddenly a gigantic steel arch appears. The feed cuts out. Other footage shows the moment of impact: an orange fireball, pricking the surrounding blackness.
Photos taken on Tuesday morning in the aftermath of the attack show a scene of watery devastation. A massive arch had tumbled overnight into the Kerch straight , with a large concrete chunk of the road crossing. Nobody will be driving across the bridge anytime soon. The adjacent railway arch span was also damaged. “We were very happy, swapping messages all night,” Leon said.
One source in Ukraine’s armed forces said the timing of the operation – hailed by Zelenskyy as “unprecedented” – was deliberate. It was conducted ahead of a meeting on Thursday between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Putin in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of an Apec summit. “The bridge is a symbol of Putin’s rule. Destroying it sends a message to the other two great leaders that Putin is not as strong as he pretends,” the person said.
They added: “We understand that what we did shows the world that the king is nude. Putin is weak and vulnerable and we just proved it. The operation was purposefully designed for this specific historic moment. Putin’s plan was to bluff at the summit about how powerful he is. In reality, he can’t even protect the most important and symbolic pillars of his regime.”
In addition to Putin’s political embarrassment before his peers, the disabling of the Kerch bridge has practical consequences. Since annexing Crimea, Russia has militarised the peninsula, effectively turning it into a giant and fortified army base. Since 2022 it has been used as a launch platform for drone and missile attacks on the port of Odesa, and other Ukrainian cities in the region.
Russia’s occupying southern army has relied on the bridge for regular deliveries of ammunition, equipment and fuel. With the crossing partially closed – rail travel reportedly reopened on Tuesday – Russia will have to use an under fire land corridor instead, connecting its Rostov oblast with the Moscow-controlled parts of Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia and Kherson provinces.
“We have disrupted their logistics to Crimea. There will be a lot of problems for Russia’s army in the south,” Leon predicted. Debris from the bridge strike is obstructing the narrow shipping corridor through the Kerch strait, linking the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea. The Azov sea now resembles a lake. Passenger ferries are unable to move, with the occupied ports of Mariupol and Berdyansk cut off.
The soldiers returned from their mission jubilant and elated. Back at their headquarters, they gathered as usual for a minute’s silence, in memory of those killed in Russia’s bloody war. “We had our daily ritual as usual. Then there were congratulations on a very successful and important operation,” Leon said. Then he added: “We are paying them back.”

articles.title_orig: American soldier held in UK suspected of spying for Russia taken into US military custody
articles.title_zh: American soldier held in UK suspected of spying for Russia taken into US military custody
articles.content_orig:
Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner was arrested by British police on 10 November over allegations related to espionage
A US soldier who was arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia has been taken into custody by the US military, police have said.
Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, 41, was detained by British counter-terrorism police ‌on 10 November in Gloucestershire over allegations relating ⁠to espionage.
The arrest was part of an investigation by UK Counter Terrorism Policing, working with authorities including the US military and the FBI.
The FBI director, Kash Patel, said in a statement on Tuesday: “This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk.
“That’s been demonstrated by the 167 counterintelligence and espionage arrests we’ve made over the last 21 months, a 53% increase.
“An army officer is in custody as the result of an espionage investigation and the close cooperation between the FBI’s Philadelphia field office and Legat London and our partners at UK Counter Terrorism Policing, MI5, UK Defence Counter Intelligence, and the US Army Counterintelligence Command. Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action.”
The suspect, a senior soldier, was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire, which serves as the headquarters of Nato’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps, the Guardian understands.
He was arrested on suspicion of offences under section 1 and section 3 of the National Security Act and was in custody at a London police station.
US authorities have said Tyner joined the military in 2008 as a senior human resources officer, and was deployed overseas to Iraq, Qatar and Afghanistan.
He was identified on Friday after British counter-terror police secured more time to question him.
As part of the investigation, officers carried out searches at two locations in Gloucestershire, the Metropolitan police said last week.
Assistant commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing: said: “Following an extensive investigation, CTP presented our case to the CPS [Crown Prosecution Service], who in turn engaged with the attorney general’s office and American partners. Subsequently, a decision was made to pass the investigation to them to progress.
“This decision was made in line with existing international protocols.
“These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place.
“I’d like to praise the excellent work of the investigation team here in the UK to get us to this point and we will continue to support our US colleagues as they take the matter forwards.”
The investigation is not linked to any other ongoing Counter Terrorism Policing investigations.
US Brig Gen Sean Stinchon said the case “should serve as a stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath we all take to protect and defend the constitution.”
He added: “Whenever we suspect somebody of betraying the trust of their fellow soldiers and jeopardising our collective defence, we will identify you, and we will ensure justice is served.
“This effort is a great example of the remarkable partnership Army Counterintelligence Command has with army prosecutors, the FBI, DOJ [Department of Justice], and the UK.”
